analysis.title: GS Kaplan - GS Global Equities Call 14 Oct 2026
key_insights: US futures mostly up small pre-open (SPX +15bps, NDX -10bps, RTY +25bps) ahead of the September US CPI print. GIR expects core CPI +0.24% m/m vs +0.2% consensus.
Crude is better bid (WTI +1.25% at $95.30) on continued Middle East tensions: reports of Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco HQ and Iran continuing to strike tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.
UST yields are little changed: 2yr -1bp at 4.775%, 10yr -1bp at 5.2%, 30yr -0.5bp at 5.55%.
China data showed strong trade numbers, hot PPI and cooler CPI.

ASML reported a solid beat and raise but faded off the highs. Bears point to no upgrade to 2027 capacity. Positives include a margin beat, a guide to higher units in 2028 and higher 2029-30 demand. Broader sentiment remains nervous.

Fed speakers are in focus after Williams' dovish remarks the day before: Bowman (voter, 5:40am), Barkin (non-voter, 1:30PM), Goolsbee (non-voter, 3PM), Bowman (voter, 10:55PM). The Fed Beige Book is due at 2PM.

September CPI preview component trends: autos inflation picks up (used cars +0.5%, new cars +0.2%, auto insurance +0.2%). Shelter is benign (OER +0.20%, rent +0.17%). Airfares +3.0% on higher jet fuel prices.

GIR expects core CPI of about +0.2% m/m in October, lifted by seasonal-factor distortions from missing data during last year's government shutdown, then about +0.1% in November and December on slowing shelter and shrinking tariff pass-through.

Hedge funds were flat globally in September. Systematic Macro/CTA funds led at +3.8%, the strategy's strongest month this year and top YTD, helped by short fixed income and long energy positions. Quant funds also did well on short-side momentum. Fundamental strategies lagged and Asia was the only region in positive territory.
Buyback desk: about 10% of corporates will be in open window by end of this week and 48% by end of month. November is the 2nd highest month for corporate repurchases on the desk.
Buyback dispersion: Energy and Utilities posted large y/y gains but are only 6% of total buybacks. Info tech buybacks are down 40% y/y and financials are up 88%.

Foreign investors own 18% of the US equity market vs 2% for hedge funds. Their positioning has been just below the 50th percentile since 2009. Midterms have historically been a catalyst for foreign buying, with inflows of about 1.75% of AUM in the six months after elections.

Mutual funds treat Halloween as their year-end. That tends to ease selling in this year's laggards for tax reasons and slow some YTD winners, a contra-momentum dynamic. October is the 3rd largest month of equity MF and ETF outflows. November and December see consecutive positive inflows.

Breadth: Bloomberg studied 13 episodes since 1995 where the 10 largest S&P stocks beat equal weight by more than 8% over three months. The median subsequent SPX return was +10.1% over six months and +19.6% over 12 months, vs historical medians of +6.9% and +15%.

CTA positioning in US equities is in the 27th percentile on a 1y lookback and 54th on a 5y lookback despite re-levering. CTAs have sold heavily in Russell stocks and are the shortest in the index since 2023.

Desk flows: activity was a 4 out of 10. HFs were moderate net buyers driven by macro products, while long-only flows skewed slightly to sell, driven by tech. Generalist and long-only outflows from Tech/AI/Memory continued, with money largely rotating out of the sector. Macro and non-traditional financials supply picked up.
Chart of the day: GS expects AI cost pressures on consumer electronics prices to add roughly 15bp to core PCE inflation over the next year.
